title: a new one-line helper that copies one another module already has
how: each new top-level one-statement function (const f = (..) => expr, or function f(..) { return expr }) of a touched file under roots, its body normalised; a finding when another module of the same group already has that body (groups: modules that can import each other; a browser module cannot import a Node one)

explain.what: A new one-line helper has the same body as a helper another module of the same group already has.
explain.why: Two copies of one helper drift apart. A fix lands in one copy, and the other keeps the bug.
explain.fix: Import the existing helper and delete the copy. If the two must differ, make the difference visible in the name or the body.

const toSlash = (p) => String(p).replace(/\\/g, '/');
export const b = q => toSlash(q) + '/';
